content:
iOS 27 beta 4 has been released today, and according to Macworld, it contains code references that likely belong to the features of a brand-new iPhone Ultra: dual batteries.

Macworld found code references in iOS 27 beta 4 corresponding to a multi-battery iPhone.

Earlier this month, Weibo leaker "數碼閒聊站" revealed that Apple's upcoming iPhone Ultra is very likely to feature not one, but two independent built-in batteries.

This kind of design is not uncommon for foldable smartphones, but it would be a first for the iPhone.

And today, following the release of iOS 27 beta 4, we have stronger evidence to support what this leaker has been saying.

Macworld's Filipe Espósito reported that the new beta version contains code strings referencing multi-battery iPhone models. He wrote:

We've previously seen quite a few references to the iPhone Ultra in the iOS 27 code. Earlier code leaks have already revealed that there will be a foldable iPhone, as well as models equipped with multiple screens.

Now, combined with the code newly discovered today, it mentions an iPhone equipped with multiple batteries.

According to regulatory filings, the two batteries have capacities of 1,921mAh and 2,962mAh respectively, totaling 4,883mAh.

All of the above supports earlier reports about the iPhone Ultra, which is expected to debut in early September.
